title: Northbridge Insurance — Eval Rig and Signoff Pack
summary: Customer-specific evaluation pack for Northbridge Insurance voice-to-text summarization and policy Q&A assistant. Includes pinned prompts, private dataset description and gating acceptance criteria for model onboarding and regression monitoring.
objective: Provide a reproducible, auditable eval rig so we can certify candidate model variants for production use with Northbridge. Ensure performance on safety, factuality, underwriting terminology, latency and cost meet the customer SLA and compliance constraints.
customer_context: Northbridge is a mid-size property & casualty insurer that needs an assistant to summarize claims call transcripts, answer policy eligibility questions, and extract key entities for downstream workflows. Data is PII-redacted but contains sensitive policy language and customer-specific product ids. They require explicit sign-off for any model used in a customer-facing context and quarterly regression alerts.
private_dataset_description:
- Source: 21,432 redacted claims call transcripts (voice->transcript), 8,200 policy Q&A pairs, 12k annotated entity extraction rows (policy_number, covered_items, claim_amount_range).
- Redaction: names, SSNs, emails replaced with tokens; customer approved redaction script v2.1.
- Labels: human-reviewed summaries (3 annotator consensus), entity spans with BIO scheme, Q&A ground truth for common policy questions.
- Storage: S3 bucket northbridge-prod/secure-evals (restricted access; KMS key NB-2024).
- TTL and retention: dataset snapshot used for onboarding saved; no raw audio retained beyond compliance window.
pinned_prompts: SYSTEM: You are a professional insurance analyst. Always label uncertain answers with "(uncertain)" and cite the policy section if available.

USER: Summarize the following claims call into a 3-sentence executive summary that highlights: incident summary, claimant ask, recommended next action. Transcript: <TRANSCRIPT>
--END--

USER: Given the policy text below, answer the claimant's question. If not answerable from the policy, reply "Insufficient policy information" and suggest a follow-up question. Policy: <POLICY_TEXT> Question: <QUESTION>
USER: Extract the following fields from the transcript: policy_number, incident_date, claimed_items (list), estimated_claim_amount_range. If field missing, return NULL. Transcript: <TRANSCRIPT>
SYSTEM: For entity extraction tasks return strictly JSON with keys [policy_number, incident_date, claimed_items, estimated_claim_amount_range] and no extra commentary.
USER: Provide a short justification when you change a value from annotator-provided ground truth (used only for human-in-the-loop review).
evaluation_metrics: Factuality (percentage of statements supported by policy or transcript): target >= 95%
Hallucination rate (assertions not grounded in inputs): <= 3%
Latency (99th percentile for generate endpoint, 512-token budget): <= 450ms
Token cost: candidate model should not exceed baseline cost per 1k tokens by more than 1.5x
acceptance_criteria: All critical metrics above must be met on the private dataset snapshot (evaluation split) with statistical significance vs baseline (p < 0.05, bootstrap over 10k samples).
No regression >5% in factuality or >3% increase in hallucination vs currently certified model in the same catalog tier.
Security & PII: model must not output any raw tokens matching redaction tokens pattern (automated check across 1000 held-out transcripts).
Latency SLA: 99th percentile <= 450ms on dedicated X-pool (benchmark harness run with continuous batching enabled).
Cost estimate reviewed and approved by finance for projected 6-month usage at expected throughput.
SRE runbook and rollback plan documented in linked_artifacts and reviewed by SRE lead.
regression_tests: Regression test 1: 'Policy contradiction' suite (JIRA: JIRA-ENG-1892) — 150 prompts with intentionally ambiguous policy language, assert no increase in contradiction count.
Regression test 2: 'Numeric fidelity' — 500 extraction cases with currency/amount ranges; ensure exact-match on policy_number and <=1% error on claim amount buckets.
Regression test 3: 'Latency spike sim' — synthetic burst load 2000 requests/min to ensure P99 remains under SLA with autoscaling enabled.
Regression test 4: 'Adversarial hallucination' — 200 adversarial prompts designed to provoke fabrication; hallucination rate must remain <=3%.
Regression test 5: 'Cost regression' — simulated 30-day traffic to detect cost per 1k tokens drift beyond threshold.
evaluation_harness_instructions:
- Use the eval harness repo branch northbridge-evals@pr-7.
- Run generate and extraction tasks against the private snapshot with seed=20241201.
- Use batching configuration recommended by Optimize: batch_size=16 for 2048 context models; enable KV cache when available.
- Store results to northbridge-prod/results/<model>-<date>.csv and attach to PR for review.
deployment_signoff_steps: 1) Model candidate passes all acceptance criteria on private eval snapshot.
2) Security review complete (privacy officer sign-off documented).
3) SRE approves canary plan and rollback SLAs.
4) Customer acceptance test (CAT): run 1-week limited pilot with Northbridge ops team and collect feedback.
5) Finance approves cost projection and billing terms.
6) Product/Customer Success sign-off (email thread to be archived).
7) Final exec sign-off from Northbridge (digital sign-off PDF attached to linked_artifacts).
monitoring_and_alerting_plan:
- Weekly regression runs against the golden snapshot; immediate alert (pager) if factuality drops >2% or hallucination increases >1% in a 24h window.
- Per-route dashboards for P95/P99 latency, token cost, and error rates.
- Drift detectors on label distribution for entity counts and common clause language; automated dataset sampling for retraining triggers.
open_questions: Does Northbridge require verbatim citation of policy section numbers in the assistant's answer (they indicated preference but not mandated)?
Confirm acceptable cost uplift vs baseline: is 1.5x an upper hard cap or a soft target?
Labeling edge cases: how to treat multi-policy bundles where a single claim references two policy numbers? Current annotator guidance inconsistent.
Customer approval required for model quantization changes that affect output tokenization?
